title: Autopsy and Confession Anew
premise: Marguerite Crane, a night-shift taxi dispatcher with a perfect record of closing every case that crosses their radio, is pulled into a murder investigation when the victim is found wearing clothes stolen from Marguerite's own closet — clothes belonging to a man who died seven years ago in a fire everyone believed was the end of it. As Marguerite reopens the case, he discovers the 'closed' death was staged by a cabal within his own company, and that his own memories of that night were surgically rewritten to make him complicit. Racing a killer who is eliminating everyone who remembers, Marguerite must reconstruct his true past from fragments — an autopsy report, a confession tape, the found family of drivers who lied to protect him — and chooses at the end to expose the truth even though it means surrendering the comfortable false life he built on it.
about_author: Astrid Ishikawa spent six years answering phones for a metropolitan taxi dispatch before turning to fiction full-time, a period she credits for her ear for voices in the dark. She writes mysteries about people whose ordinary jobs place them one wrong call away from catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Last Fare
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A routine night shift: we learn the rules of dispatch, Marguerite's pride in never losing a case, and the small found family of night drivers. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Wrong Address
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Police arrive at the depot: a body found in a drainage culvert wearing Marguerite's own missing coat and shirt. Detective Okafor questions him; the clothes are identified by monogram. Beat: disbelief curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Man Who Burned
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, flashback-tinged. The victim is identified as Elias Vann — declared dead seven years ago in the depot fire Marguerite barely survived. Beat: vertigo as a closed past cracks open.

chapters.title: Everyone Swore
chapters.summary: Multiple short testimonies framed through Marguerite's POV: coworkers insist Elias died, the fire was accidental, the case closed. Marguerite notices they all use identical phrasing. Beat: creeping suspicion of choreography.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Closet
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Searching his apartment, he finds other items missing — items tied to the fire's aftermath. Someone has access. Beat: violation; home becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Okafor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Detective Okafor POV. She doesn't believe Marguerite is guilty but can't rule him out; her private file shows the original fire investigation was shut down from above. Beat: institutional rot glimpsed.

chapters.title: The Night Book
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He pulls the dispatch logs from the fire night and finds pages excised — cut cleanly, professionally. Beat: determination hardening into obsession.

chapters.title: Driver 12
chapters.summary: Sasha, veteran driver and Marguerite's closest friend, POV. She recognizes something in the new case and quietly destroys a personal record before anyone asks. Beat: loyalty at war with guilt.

chapters.title: Autopsy Report, Annotated
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A leaked autopsy shows Elias died recently — not seven years ago — and bears old surgical scarring consistent with memory-altering intervention. Beat: horror reframed; Marguerite wonders what was done to him too.

chapters.title: Confession, First Draft
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He finds a cassette labeled in his own handwriting: 'Confession — do not play.' He plays it; his own voice confesses to something he cannot remember doing. Beat: self-betrayal.

chapters.title: The Company Man
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV (unnamed executive). We see the machinery: a compliance officer monitoring dispatch, a list of names being crossed off. Beat: cold menace; the reader knows more than Marguerite.

chapters.title: Fare Evasion
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Someone follows him between stops; he uses dispatcher tricks to shake the tail and realizes whoever hunts him knows the radio codes. Beat: paranoia sharpening into tradecraft.

chapters.title: What Sasha Knew
chapters.summary: Sasha POV. Confronted gently by Marguerite, she admits she drove Elias away from the depot the night of the fire — on orders she never questioned. Beat: found family fracturing under old obedience.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The former fire investigator is found dead, staged identically — wearing another driver's clothes. Pattern confirmed: the killer dresses victims in the wardrobes of the living. Beat: dread; the killer is speaking to them.

chapters.title: Dress Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Okafor POV. She maps the pattern: each victim costumed as someone still alive, meaning the next body will wear someone's life. Marguerite's closet was a message — he's on the list. Beat: urgency ignites.

chapters.title: Night Shift, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Dispatch receives a call from a voice that sounds exactly like Elias, giving an address, then silence. Beat: grief weaponized; hope and trap indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Address
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The address leads to a shuttered clinic where the fire's survivors were treated. He finds patient intake forms — including his own name, dated after the fire. Beat: identity destabilized.

chapters.title: Memory, Itemized
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, fragmented structure. His memories of the fire don't match physical evidence: no smoke smell, wrong exits, borrowed details. Beat: mourning a self that may be manufactured.

chapters.title: The Drivers' Union
chapters.summary: Ensemble scene via alternating driver POVs. The night crew meets secretly; some want to protect Marguerite, others want him to stop digging. Beat: found family tested, splitting into factions.

chapters.title: Paper Trail, Burning
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The clinic records are destroyed in a suspicious fire hours before he can return. The arsonist's method matches the original depot fire. Beat: history literally repeating; rage.

chapters.title: Confession, Second Draft
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A second tape appears in his locker — this time not his voice, but Elias's, recorded before the first 'death,' naming names inside the company. Beat: the case reopens with teeth.

chapters.title: The Names
chapters.summary: Okafor POV. Cross-referencing Elias's list with personnel files: three executives, one doctor, and one redacted name that makes her go pale. Beat: conspiracy scaled up; stakes become systemic.

chapters.title: Safe House Radio
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He and Sasha go dark, running dispatch from a parked cab, using the radio network as an invisible office. Beat: warmth amid danger — the found family's best night.

chapters.title: The Doctor's Waiting Room
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He tracks the clinic's surgeon, Dr. Imre Hale, who admits performing 'therapeutic revision' on fire witnesses — including Marguerite — paid for by the company. Beat: devastating confirmation; Marguerite's whole life is a cover story.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, intimate and slow. Hale's notes reveal what was removed: Marguerite witnessed the company torching the depot to destroy evidence, and he loved someone who died there. Beat: grief for stolen love and stolen truth.

chapters.title: Hale, Silenced
chapters.summary: Okafor POV. Dr. Hale is found dead before testifying, dressed in Okafor's spare blazer from her car. The killer is inside the investigation. Beat: betrayal at close range; trust collapses.

chapters.title: The Redacted Name
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Working from Hale's partial notes, Marguerite decodes the redaction: the fifth name is his own — listed not as witness but as participant. Beat: darkest hour; the confession tapes begin to make terrible sense.

chapters.title: Confession, Final Draft
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He pieces it together: coerced under threat, pre-revision Marguerite agreed to sign a false confession taking blame for the fire, then had his memory erased so he'd believe it if it ever surfaced. Beat: compassion for his past self; resolve reborn.

chapters.title: Turn the Meter On
chapters.summary: Sasha POV. She rallies the drivers: every cabbie in the fleet becomes Marguerite's eyes, flooding the company's surveillance with noise. Beat: found family fully mobilized; hope with engines.

chapters.title: The Executive Floor
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He infiltrates headquarters during a night event, reaching the archive where the original fire evidence was stored. Beat: thriller tempo; doors, badges, held breath.

chapters.title: Ash and Ledger
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He finds the intact ledger proving the fire was ordered to bury embezzlement — and a current order authorizing 'asset resolution' for remaining witnesses. Beat: proof in hand; countdown begun.

chapters.title: Caught on Camera
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. The compliance officer, Mr. Voss, watches Marguerite on security feeds and lets him leave — because a panicked thief is easier to frame than a careful witness. Beat: the trap closes elegantly.

chapters.title: Framed
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Warrants issue for his arrest; planted evidence mirrors the costume killings. Okafor must choose between procedure and belief. Beat: everything lost in a single news cycle.

chapters.title: The Ride
chapters.summary: Okafor POV. Marguerite surrenders to Okafor alone, in her car, and gives her the ledger plus a copy hidden in the dispatch system itself — broadcast in fragments across routine fare calls. Beat: trust as a calculated gamble.

chapters.title: Signal Lost
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In holding, he listens as the drivers execute the plan: the buried evidence streams through dispatch channels to a hundred simultaneous recipients, including press. Beat: tension at maximum; the network fights back.

chapters.title: Voss Descends
chapters.summary: Voss POV. Exposed, he attempts to erase Marguerite personally — the final loose end — staging one last costume killing with Marguerite as both victim and wardrobe. Beat: predator cornered, most dangerous.

chapters.title: Dispatch, Live
chapters.summary: Climax, Marguerite's POV. Voss takes him to the old depot; using the emergency radio band, Marguerite broadcasts their location mid-struggle while stalling with everything he's learned. Drivers and Okafor converge. Beat: courage; the voice in the dark saves itself.

chapters.title: Arrest and Aftermath
chapters.summary: Resolution, mixed POVs. Voss and the executives are arrested; the tapes, ledger, and a hundred witnesses end the cover-up. Marguerite's coerced confession is voided. Beat: exhale; justice is procedural but real.

chapters.title: Memory, Restored
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. With therapy and Sasha's corroboration, he reintegrates the erased months — grieving the person who died in the fire, forgiving the self who survived. Beat: sorrow and integration; the price of survival named.

chapters.title: Autopsy and Confession Anew
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Marguerite's POV. He returns to the night shift by choice, takes a call from a scared stranger, and closes one more case — but now keeps a wall of photographs of those he lost and found. Beat: peace earned, not given; the family answers when he calls.
